subject: literature
passage: Every summer, Ines helped her grandfather sort the old photographs he kept in a shoebox under his bed. He had never labeled a single one, yet he could name every face. He held up a picture of a young woman standing beside a bicycle and smiled. "This ______ he said, "is your grandmother at nineteen."
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.why: The grandfather's sentence, "This is your grandmother at nineteen," is interrupted by "he said." The first part of the quotation ends with a comma, and in American English that comma goes inside the closing quotation mark.
explanation.A: Incorrect. A comma is needed to separate the quotation from the speaker tag "he said."
explanation.B: Correct. The comma before "he said" goes inside the closing quotation mark, as American English requires.
explanation.C: Incorrect. In American English, a comma always goes inside the closing quotation mark, not outside it.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The quoted sentence continues after "he said," so the first part can't end with a period.
